headline_marked: [[LLMS.TXT]] is NOT an AI Search Tactic, Data Shows
headline: LLMS.TXT is NOT an AI Search Tactic, Data Shows
summary: Four independent studies and Google's own guide reveal that the llms.txt file has negligible impact on AI search visibility. Learn why it's considered noise.
details: The llms.txt file was promoted as a way to help AI search engines like ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews find and understand your website's best content. However, extensive data from multiple studies suggests this is not the case.

Google's official guide on optimizing for generative AI features in Search, published in May 2026, explicitly states that "You don't need to create new machine readable files... to appear in generative AI search." This echoes sentiments from Google's John Mueller, who noted over a year prior that AI services do not appear to be using llms.txt.

Despite Google's Chrome team including an llms.txt check in Lighthouse's experimental Agentic Browsing audits, Mueller clarified that it's "not done for search" and is more of a "temporary crutch" for AI coding tools parsing developer documentation.

Ahrefs analyzed access logs and found that major AI bots overwhelmingly crawl HTML directly, not llms.txt. Their data also revealed a crawler identifying as "prompt-injection-survey/1.0," suggesting systematic study of llms.txt as a potential prompt injection vector.

Further analysis by SE Ranking and OtterlyAI corroborated these findings. SE Ranking's study showed that removing the llms.txt variable actually improved prediction accuracy for AI citation, indicating it was noise, not a signal. OtterlyAI found its impact on AI crawler behavior to be "marginal at best."

Limy's extensive analysis of over 515 million AI bot traffic events over 90 days confirmed that the bots most relevant for AI search visibility "overwhelmingly skip the file and crawl HTML directly." The share of AI bot traffic interacting with llms.txt was "statistically negligible."

The consensus from these studies and Google's own guidance is clear: focus on creating valuable, non-commodity content. If an AI can write your article itself, it will likely not cite you because it already possesses the information.

headline_marked: Microsoft Overhauls [[Windows 11 Search]] for Speed and Capability
headline: Microsoft Overhauls Windows 11 Search for Speed and Capability
summary: A redesigned Windows Search is in testing, promising significant improvements in performance, memory usage, and user interface.
details: Microsoft is rolling out a significantly overhauled Windows Search experience for Windows 11, focusing on speed and enhanced capabilities. This update aims to address long-standing frustrations with the search functionality in the operating system.

The new search is built on WinUI 3 and is designed for speed, with early testing showing substantial improvements in performance and memory usage. The user interface has also been modernized with speedy animations and a large preview pane for files.

Beyond visual enhancements, Microsoft is improving the underlying search engine to better understand user queries, including improved matching for typos and synonyms. This aims to make finding information more intuitive and accurate.

A key feature is the ability for the new Windows Search to act as a launcher, taking actions like toggling Bluetooth or dark mode, minimizing windows, or opening apps side-by-side. It can even integrate with Phone Link to send texts directly from search.

This new Windows Search interface is currently being tested with Windows Insiders. Microsoft plans to integrate it into the Start menu next year, adapting it to various taskbar positions and configurations to make Windows Search more capable and user-friendly.
